questions.stem: When should a Metadata Strategy take place relative to project or product strategies?
options: Only after the first dashboards have gone live
Alongside them, and the earlier the better
After the Data Lake has been fully populated
Once Data Lineage problems have appeared
At the end of the project, as a documentation exercise
questions.explanation: Metadata Strategy should run along with project or product strategies, meaning the earlier the better.

questions.stem: By roughly how much can Metadata and Master Data reduce an organisation's BI footprint?
options: They cannot reduce it at all
questions.explanation: Well-described Metadata means a new BI report is only generated when an earlier one does not serve the purpose, which can cut the BI footprint by 80%.

questions.stem: Which everyday example illustrates Metadata as the index of a book?
options: The index indicates which page contains which topic
The index lists every word in the book alphabetically
The index is the longest chapter of the book
The index holds the raw text of each chapter
The index is the ISBN printed on the cover
questions.explanation: The index of a book is Metadata because it indicates which page contains which topic; the acknowledgment page is another example.

questions.stem: Which type of metadata covers business definitions, descriptions, data models, data quality rules and data standards?
questions.explanation: Business Metadata covers the solution implementation from a business view, such as definitions, descriptions, data model, data quality rules and data standards.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of Operational Metadata?
options: A job's execution date, duration and error alerts
An access permission on a table
questions.explanation: Operational Metadata is about the execution result of an implemented solution, for example execution date, error alerts and job duration.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT listed among the types of metadata?
options: Metadata about database, table and column names
questions.explanation: The three types are Business, Technical and Operational Metadata; database, table and column names belong to Technical Metadata.

questions.stem: What happens to data if Metadata is not in place and Data Lineage therefore cannot be figured out?
options: The data becomes a Data Swamp
The data is compressed to save space
questions.explanation: Without Metadata you cannot figure out Data Lineage, and without Data Lineage your Data becomes a Data Swamp.

questions.stem: In a metadata architecture, what is the Metadata Portal?
options: The centralised store that holds metadata from all source systems
The layer exposed for users to search metadata
The high-level model of connections between systems
The individual repository hosting metadata at the source side
The ETL job that loads metadata overnight
questions.explanation: The Metadata Portal is the layer exposed for users to search metadata, whereas the Enterprise Metadata Repository is the centralised store.

questions.stem: In a Distributed Metadata Architecture, which capability is NOT available?
options: Connecting the portal to source metadata repositories
Hosting metadata at the source side
questions.explanation: In a Distributed Metadata Architecture there is no enterprise metadata repository, so the portal connects directly to source repositories and cross-system search is not available.

questions.stem: Which metadata architecture is described as the most complex, with metadata pulled from source systems and pushed back to them after updates?
questions.explanation: Bi-Directional Metadata Architecture is the most complex: changes flow both ways so both repositories stay up to date all the time.
